transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I need help getting them to stop monitoring me. Everywhere I go, there are people following me and sending coded signals to each other about what I'm doing. I just don't know who to trust anymore with this constant surveillance.

Have you also had times when your mood was unusually high or irritable with lots of energy and little need for sleep, or times when you felt very depressed for days to weeks? If so, did the monitoring experiences happen only during those mood episodes or even when your mood felt normal?

No, I've never experienced those kinds of extreme highs or deep depressions. My mood has generally been normal, aside from the constant stress of being watched all the time. The monitoring happens constantly, no matter how I'm feeling.

Aside from feeling watched, have you had other problems like hearing voices, your thoughts getting jumbled, or a big decline in work, school, or taking care of yourself? Or is this mainly the fixed belief that people are monitoring you while the rest of your thinking and daily functioning stay about the same?

No, I don't hear any voices and my thoughts aren't jumbled at all. I still go to work and take care of my daily responsibilities just fine. The only issue is this constant surveillance, but otherwise my thinking and life are completely normal.
How long have you been convinced that people are monitoring you? Has this belief been present for at least one month?
Yes, it has been going on for much longer than just a month. I have been constantly monitored for about two years and two months now. It started back then and hasn't stopped for a single day.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Delusional Disorder"], and based on this conversation the list remains the same. This pattern continues to support Delusional Disorder over schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder with psychotic features, or major depressive disorder with psychotic features.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, fixed belief of being monitored and followed for over two years, consistent with a persecutory delusion. There is no evidence of mood episodes, hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked functional decline, which supports Delusional Disorder over schizophrenia spectrum or mood disorders with psychotic features.
